analysis: Portfolio is nearly fully deployed with only $3,112 (3% of equity) in available cash. The three existing positions (MCO, MSFT, V) are all quality names already in the screened universe, all profitable, and all in uptrending/basing setups — thesis intact on all three. MSFT is already well over the 25% single-name cap at ~49% of equity (legacy sizing), so no adds there. V at ~24% and MCO at ~24% are at the concentration ceiling. The fundamental problem: with only $3,112 in cash, proper position sizing is impossible. The formula (equity * 0.015 / stop_distance) produces required share counts that far exceed available cash for any candidate. Even the cheapest quality candidates (KVUE ~$18, PRU ~$100) would produce a position so small (under $3,112 cost) that the portfolio risk contribution would be negligible (under 0.1% of equity) — a rounding error, not a conviction trade. Forcing a tiny fourth position just to deploy $3K would violate the spirit of concentrated high-conviction investing. The screened list does contain genuinely attractive setups — FDS at 18% of 52w range with a low fwd P/E of 12, NVDA still extending but with huge EPS revision momentum, ZBRA basing with PEG 0.53 — but these require real capital to matter. The correct action is to hold cash, let existing winners run, and wait for either (a) a position to be closed freeing capital, or (b) the portfolio to generate enough gains to fund a properly-sized new position. Cash is a position. Forcing trades is the enemy.
